analysis.title: UBS House View Monthly Extended November 2026
key_insights: UBS CIO keeps an Attractive absolute view on global, US, Europe, Eurozone, Switzerland, UK, EM, Japan and Asia ex-Japan equities. Strong earnings growth is the main support, led by AI investment, despite higher bond yields, elevated energy prices and geopolitical risk.

The base case (50%) for June 2027 is Resilient growth: S&P 500 8,400 (+8% from 7,805), MSCI AC World 1,510 (+10%), EuroStoxx 50 7,100, MSCI EM 1,920, US 10y yield 4.75%, Fed funds upper bound 4.50. Bull case Goldilocks 25% (S&P 500 9,500), Bear I yield reset 15% (S&P 500 7,000), Bear II AI bear market 10% (S&P 500 5,500).

The bull case assumes AI spending and adoption beat expectations and the Strait of Hormuz reopens quickly. The base case assumes AI investment stays solid for 12 months and Hormuz traffic resumes gradually with setbacks. Bear I assumes prolonged Hormuz disruption and fiscal pressure on European bond yields. Bear II assumes AI stocks deflate on weak return-on-investment concerns.

UBS expects third-quarter S&P 500 earnings-per-share growth of 25-30%, supported by AI investment, an improving industrial cycle and healthy consumption. Investors should stay invested with diversified cyclical and structural exposure and use strength to reduce concentrated single-stock and excess US tech positions.

Asset class preferences: equities, fixed income and commodities are all Attractive in absolute terms, and all In line in relative terms. Within equities, the Eurozone, Asia ex-Japan and EM are Preferred, Switzerland and the UK are Least preferred. Within bonds, EM is Preferred and high grade is Least preferred. In commodities, copper is Preferred and silver is Least preferred.

Equity sectors: US Attractive in Consumer Discretionary, Financials, Health Care, Industrials and Utilities, Neutral in Info Technology. Europe Attractive in Consumer Discretionary, Banks, Health Care, Industrials and Info Technology. Themes rated Attractive include AI, Power and resources, Longevity, European leaders, Global Luxury & Lifestyles, Automation and Robotics and Swiss mid-caps.

Central banks have turned hawkish and are hiking. In September the Fed, ECB and BoJ all raised rates in the same month, a historical first. Energy-driven inflation from the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine conflicts is feeding into official prints with second-round effects in some goods and services.
Two new market developments: French government bonds underperformed, and questions rose over whether AI capex and returns can meet expectations as financing costs for several AI players rose sharply.

US 10y Treasury yield hit a cycle high of 5.36% in early October, then fell sharply in a risk-off move centered on financing of AI capex. UBS expects 10y yields to settle in a 4.5-5% range. The market prices another 75bps of Fed tightening, which UBS sees as beyond its base case of 'recalibration hikes'.

US fixed income: the 2-5y Treasury segment is the best risk-reward, but a higher term premium makes selective extension toward the 10y area reasonable for diversification. It would take a 113bps rise in 5y Treasury yields for capital losses to offset a year of income.

Europe bonds: Bunds outperformed on flight to quality as French OAT spreads widened. UBS sees market expectations of 75bps more ECB tightening as unlikely to be realized and the ECB possibly needing to address balance sheet policy to ease spread stress. UK: nearly 125bps of BoE hikes are priced at the front end, a 28 October Budget is expected to show fiscal continuity, and UBS sees scope for tactical extension toward 10y gilts. Switzerland: 50bps of SNB hikes priced is reasonable.

Credit: IG spreads widened only 10bps in a month, with yields of 5.7% USD and 4.2% EUR. High yield spreads widened about 50bps to near 330bps in the US and EUR markets. US HY returned -2.49% and EUR HY -1.79%, the weakest month since September 2022. CCC spreads are above 1,000bps, BB +43bps and B +55bps. HY yields are about 8.3% (US) and 6.7% (EUR).

AI credit exposure: hyperscaler bonds are about 4% of the US IG Intermediate index and are mostly rated AA or higher with debt capacity. AI-linked data center issuers are about 3% of US high yield. Heavy hyperscaler supply may cause some indigestion and moderately wider spreads.

FX: UBS expects the USD to weaken over the medium term as the recent rally looks stretched and positioning is skewed long USD. EURUSD fell from about 1.17 to near 1.11 and looks oversold, with a 1.16 year-end target. GBP, NOK and CNY are Attractive versus USD, and CHF is the preferred funding currency for long GBP, NOK and CNY positions. Neutral on USDJPY, expected in a 155-160 range as the Fed and BoJ keep hiking.
EM FX carry: UBS favors diversified exposure to MXN, ZAR, BRL and INR, with FX implied volatility back toward normal ranges after an extended period near multiyear lows.

Commodities: the CMCI Commodity Total Return Index is up more than 30% year to date. Copper is the preferred metal on tight mine supply and concentrate, falling LME and SHFE inventories, and electrification demand. Aluminum is also favored, while zinc, nickel and lead are viewed cautiously. Cobre Panama restart headlines have no clarity on timing.

Gold is Neutral, spot USD 4,153/oz with a base case June 2027 target of USD 4,700 (bull 5,200, bear II 6,000, bull-case-implied USD 3,800). UBS sees structural dip buyers near USD 4,000/oz, expects central bank purchases of 750-1,000 metric tons a year, and recommends a mid-single-digit gold allocation.

Oil: Middle East exports have recovered but remain below pre-conflict levels, leaving the market undersupplied. OECD strategic reserve releases give only temporary relief and may raise future price volatility. Oil is Neutral.

US economy base case (60%): 1H26 growth revised to 2.4% annualized, 3Q GDP tracking about 3.2%, moderating toward 2.0%. September CPI was 3.7% y/y headline and 2.6% core, core PCE is tracking about 3.1%. UBS expects Fed hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 and then a hold until late 2027.

Eurozone base case: GDP growth of 0.8% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027, headline inflation reaching 4% by early 2027, and one more ECB hike in December with the risk of further tightening high. The ECB should resume easing in late 2027.
Swiss economy: GDP growth of 1.8% in 2026 and 1.5% in 2027, inflation 1% in September, with two SNB hikes forecast in March and June 2027 taking the policy rate to 0.5%.

China: third-quarter GDP grew 4.5% y/y, exports rose 28.4% y/y, retail sales grew 0.7% and fixed-asset investment contracted 10.0%. September PPI hit a 51-month high of 5.0% y/y and CPI was 0.9%. The Trump-Xi September summit extended the trade truce with targeted tariff cuts.

Global economy: developed-market consumers are drawing down savings to absorb higher prices from tariffs and the Gulf war. Because the inflation is mainly an oil shock, central banks are expected to stay at the top of the neutral range rather than turn restrictive.

Equity AI risk watchlist: compute supply-demand dynamics are the key indicator, with GPU rental prices still pointing to a strong market. Watchpoints are enterprise productivity returns, private capital access, power availability, data center permitting and hyperscaler cash flows. Financing stress is greater for new compute suppliers than for hyperscalers.

Capital preservation strategies are suggested for investors with concentrated positions or low loss tolerance. UBS also suggests putting cash to work, phasing into diversified portfolios, and using hedge funds (low net equity long/short, macro, multi-strategy, merger arbitrage) and private markets (infrastructure, secondaries, value buyout) as diversifiers.

earnings_insights: UBS expects third-quarter 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth of 25-30% (UBS estimate, not yet reported), driven by AI investment, an improving industrial cycle and consumption.
UBS forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027, citing a cyclical recovery tied to AI, electrification, defense spending and reshoring.
UBS says hyperscalers have kept aggressive capex plans and are seeing increasing returns on them, and that Asia and EM should deliver some of the strongest earnings growth globally.

trade_ideas.description: Capital preservation strategies and structured equity participation for investors with concentrated positions
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong earnings support equities, but rates, energy, geopolitics and AI monetization could cause volatility.

risk_factors: Further Middle East escalation or prolonged Hormuz disruption pushing energy prices higher.
More aggressive Fed tightening than the 75bps priced in, or a bond yield spike.
AI capex returns disappointing and rising financing costs for AI players.
French and wider European fiscal and sovereign spread stress.
US tariffs and trading partner retaliation after the midterms.
Hyperscaler bond supply causing spread widening, and weak CCC credit conditions.
Oil strategic reserve drawdowns leaving the market more exposed to future disruptions.
vol_and_positioning: FX implied volatility has moved back toward normal historical ranges after an extended period near multiyear lows; carry trades remain favored.
Positioning is heavily skewed toward further USD strength, which UBS sees as stretched.
October risk-off move in equities and credit centered on AI capex financing sent 10y yields down from the 5.36% cycle high.
High-quality bonds again show negative correlation with risk assets, giving portfolio protection when growth fears rise.
geopolitical: Strait of Hormuz disruption and the Gulf/US-Iran war keep oil flows below pre-conflict levels and drive energy inflation.
Russia-Ukraine conflict continues, with a ceasefire in the bull case and intensification in the bear case.
US effective tariff rate of 10-15% globally and 30-40% on China in the base case, with the risk of a higher rate after the November midterm elections.
Trump-Xi summit in September extended the trade truce with targeted tariff cuts and dialogue on AI.
French fiscal concerns and widening OAT spreads.
US midterm elections in early November add political uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers keep aggressive capex and see rising returns, GPU rental prices point to strong compute demand, and Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth is expected at 25-30%. UBS puts the base case S&P 500 at 8,400.
tension_points.bear_case: Financing costs for AI players have risen sharply, and the AI bear case (10%) has the S&P 500 at 5,500 if returns on investment disappoint and capex falls.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of weak enterprise productivity returns, loss of private capital access, or power and permitting bottlenecks undermining AI capex.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields near 20-year highs offer income and a cushion; UBS expects 10y yields to settle in 4.5-5% and policy expectations to be too hawkish.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy pass-through may delay the return to 2% inflation, and the market already prices 75bps more tightening. The Yield reset bear case (15%) has the 10y at 5.50%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Pricing beyond UBS 'recalibration hikes' or a 10y Treasury yield sustained above the 5.36% cycle high.
